newsitem.title: UK: Med oil products steady, fuel oil looks eastwards.
newsitem.headline: Med oil products steady, fuel oil looks eastwards.

text.p: Mediterranean oil product markets were largely steady on Friday, though fuel oil was boosted by attempts to take material eastwards.
Gasoline was steady despite modest gains in the U.S. and a $2 a tonne rise in barge swaps.
Dealers said the arbitrage to the U.S. remained closed and saw little local demand from West Africa.

Naphtha swayed with the fortunes of crude on Friday in a thin trading day. The market fundamentally looks increasingly long and with the arbitrage window to Asia firmly closed the threat of building supplies looms, traders said.
Gas oil was steady with dealers looking to the recently awarded Syrian and Turkish tenders, four and two cargoes respectively, to give support.
Russian 0.2 pct cargoes hovered near high fob quotes +$1.50 while Italian barrels were looking for high fob quotes +$2-3.
Russian supplies have been thinned out by increased domestic agricultural demand which has helped to limit the drop in premiums which resulted when the Asian arbitrage window closed.
Fuel oil markets were boosted by buying activity connected to reported attempts to move material to the Far East where high sulphur swap values have soared to $103/$104.
Recent bunker buying has also helped lift Mediterranean values, though bid levels heard to be $79 fob were being dismissed as out of line with reality.
However, 45,000 tonnes of 360-cst material was heard bought from Cartagena at $80.50 fob, reportedly for eastward trans-shipment.
Traders said there was still some bunker demand into Algeciras and Las Palmas, with the latter hard to fill at the price the buyer was willing to pay.
Russian fuel oil was still struggling to find purchasers.
